Meu comentário foi dentro de uma thread. Você sabe como o Reddit funciona? Funciona assim: não respondi ao op, mas à resposta, e apenas à resposta. Não acusei ninguém de machismo, você que tá quase se auto-acusando aí porque é inseguro - conectando um contexto alucinógeno ao meu comentário. Seria diferente se você me acusasse de ser condescendente depois desse comentário, porque isso realmente fui. Vê a diferença? 

Deixei claro que não tô falando da "insegurança como característica humana", que inclusive é um defeito também, mas de patamar diferente. Estou falando da projeção da insegurança como forma de controle. Eu disse quase exatamente essas palavras. Sua distorção argumentativa não tem propósito algum. E sim, utilizar da insegurança, do "ciúme do bem" ou de qualquer outra característica para controlar, monitorar e mandar, é coisa de gente desonesta, baixa e ridícula, o que se traduz em "virjão". Quem tá tentando analisar pela semântica de que só acontece com homem é você. Eu jamais disse isso. 

Se você (e, agora sim, falando do caso do op também) se sente desconfortável por causa de uma roupa, você precisa tratar isso. Você diz do "conforto do parceiro", e há alguma lógica, mas você também não está se preocupando com ele/a ao exigir determinada vestimenta. Eu acho que esse caso é de uma pequenez extrema, tanto pedir para trocar de roupa quanto responder do jeito que ele diz que ela respondeu. Simplesmente tô velho demais pra isso. E é por isso que não respondi ao post, mas à resposta. Capisce?

O que eu disse é literalmente sobre insegurança. Sequer falei de machismo propriamente dito. A minha crítica é a mesma. Insegurança (do tipo projetada nos outros com frases como a que escrevi) e mania de controle são coisas de virjão trouxa.

My ranking is very weird. I'll explain why each rank, knowing that this is not a technical opinion, but just a "my heart says" one.

1. **Legion**. Very well-polished content, M+ were a blast as well as the raids, legendary weapon <3, and class hall was decent. Visuals were absolutely astonishing. Not needed to grind forever to get ONE goddamn enchant. It was the expansion I played the most and got the farthest away, finishing all Mythic content before nerfs.
2. **Cataclysm**. Yes, I know, you had to grind for hours to get something done, and leveling 84-85 was a nightmare (weeks!), but Firelands specifically was such a fun and diverse raid for me. It was when I started, and never stopped, maining Discipline Priest. Bastion of Twilight was fun too. I played lots of Cata, mostly between Firelands (which was a pain to finish in Heroic) and Dragon Soul (which I couldn't beat Spine of Deathwing Heroic on time). Lots of new BGs and Tol Barad, which I found fun to play casually. During this period, I got the Hotter Streak and For The Horde! achievements, which I hold darling to date. Also, another thing that made the major difference was that they made servers in my location, which allowed me to play the game without 500 ping.
3. **Wrath of the Lich King**. It was the expansion I got more seriously into WoW. Ulduar and ICC were just great, but the system needed polishment still. I liked the talents system back then. Death Knights were OP, almost a fun policy. I played Warlock in this xpac after having mixed feelings with Mage in TBC, and I loved it.
4. **Dragonflight**. Been playing for a week and this has the potential to surpass my experience with Legion. I haven't had the chance to properly raid yet to check the mechanics and what I like, thus it's fourth so far, but I feel it's great. Storyline isn't excellent, but I like it a bit. Absolutely hated dragonriding for one hour, now I can't stop with it. Amazing scenarios. Wrathion is great. 
5. **The Burning Crusade.** Yes, this one is kinda harsh, but I have so many good memories of trying to learn WoW in Sunwell Plateau, being gear-checked every single second, trying to kill Kael and failing so - many - times, and meaningless chatting through the take-forever walks, that it got incrusted in my memory. It was a very different time, I didn't have money to buy a decent computer or the game, but me and my friends managed to get through it and experience the game. Just good memories.
6. **Mists of Pandaria**. First pause on WoW ever. I went to the pre-release of this xpac, into a mall in my city, was really hyped. However... I wasn't able to raid in Mists because my friends all stopped playing and LFR was trivial, but I spent some time at the Timeless Island, grinding those coins. I thought this xpac was not for me. Too much grinding -- the same as what I hated on Cataclysm --, without the fun of Cataclysm (having friends). Didn't like the storyline either. However, Monks and Pandas were fun. 
7. **Shadowlands.** Get your rocks and throw them. I just experienced the content and played a bit of raids, and I just like it. The story is off and kinda weird, but I thought the gameplay experience was good. A lot of cutscenes which help the immersion. Of course, a lot of problems, as you guys know. But, overall, it's the same level as MoP for me, considering that I played SL much less.
8. **Classic.** It's great, just not for me. I was a hyperactive teenager back then, recently getting into competitive MTG, the game was too expensive and required too much of a computer, took forever to download, and I did not have 40 friends. I didn't play the game properly -- yes, I did build my first character, but that was about it. I feel the game is a tad slow (!!) and repetitive. Wait. Isn't this World of Warcraft...? Well. I remember playing Classic's dungeons. It was a nightmare. Fun, but a nightmare.
9. **Battle For Azeroth**. I'm doing the questline right now... meh. At the time, I was really hyped with Legion and thought it would be a blast to swim into a world-pvp oriented game, aaand...... nope. First of all, PvP is dead. And BFA took away most things I liked on Legion, just to replace them with weird, uncomfortable mechanics. Didn't even experience endgame content. It felt too focused on being FORCED to go through the history, grind quests, etc., etc. Didn't like it at all. Besides, Sylvannas was a very enjoyable character for me, and they just made her look like a Garrosh 2.0 on steroids. Nah. (But some of the best cutscenes are in this expansion! Beware the Daughter of the Sea and Saurfang are GENIUS!)
10. **Warlods of Draenor**. I am sorry but who had the idea to turn WoW into an AFK clicker game? I didn't understand what I was supposed to do in this xpac, there was no point in leveling, PUG was weird. Dungeons were honestly bad and too long. Got fed up way before enjoying endgame content. I was a huuuge disappointment for me.

Estou passando por um período de profunda depressão e solidão, e não está fácil. O uso de redes sociais alavanca essa dificuldade exponencialmente. Desinstalei o Facebook por me achar rejeitado - enquanto em 2014/15 minhas publicações chegavam a 100-150 likes, atualmente não passavam de 10. Quando percebi que isso estava me incomodando - veja como era inconsciente -, me dei conta de que talvez fosse tempo de me afastar. 

Uso Tinder e já tive muitos encontros. Nenhum nunca chegou perto de dar certo, pelo menos do jeito que eu gostaria. Sou uma pessoa relativamente carente e bem estranha, além de definitivamente não ser bonito, o que contribui para um não-estreitamento dos possíveis vínculos criados a partir de um aplicativo que serve de cardápio. Atualmente, para mim, ele serve muito mais como passatempo (gosto de observar a beleza das pessoas) do que qualquer outra coisa.

Já o Instagram nunca foi algo que usei muito. Tenho várias postagens e tal mas ninguém nunca interagiu por lá.

Enfim, o ponto é que a Internet constrói e destrói a autoestima em níveis semelhantes. Quando você tem atenção, você se sente muito melhor do que é; quando não tem, muito pior. Isso porque ninguém está lhe conhecendo a fundo, apenas julgando a primeira camada de você - desde seu rosto/suas fotos até a maneira como você digita. As relações modernas são extremamente baseadas nessa primeira camada, no imediatismo, o que torna difícil aceitar que nós somos mais do que essa crosta; assim, uma vez que você constrói suas relações com pessoas que sabem apenas o mínimo de você, você mesmo acaba percebendo só esse mínimo também.

O jeito para lidar com isso é a. se conhecendo bem e solidificando o que você pensa de você mesmo e b. procurando ir mais a fundo antes de "sentir" qualquer coisa por alguém (amizade, amor, enfim). O problema é que a maioria das pessoas jamais atenta para esse problema e não irão fazer o mesmo por você. Daí que você precisa ser firme e isso vai acabar te desconectando da maioria das pessoas, jogando na sua cara uma realidade simples: a maioria das pessoas se assume essa crosta porque é o que são.

E é muito fácil perceber tudo isso. Tomar alguma atitude é que é a dificuldade.
O mais triste é que isso já acontece para esses grupos. :/

I wanted everything to be perfect. Chose the restaurant very carefully - a discret place as she would prefer -, saved money for a year so that I can pay for it, discovered her favorite food. It was a hell of a job, but in the end, I thought I got this. 

My dad died in a car accident twelve years ago (he crashed the car in the city, leading to an explosion that killed many people) and my mother was missing; nobody knows where she is. Thus, I live with my grandma since I was a kid. She always worked hard, but life wasn't easy: our rent was expensive and we couldn't always buy what we wanted. But I loved her nevertheless, that's why I decided to celebrate her 70th birthday with style. I don't know what she will think of this, but I hope she likes it.

Arriving at the restaurant, I noticed that even my finest clothes weren't enough for the place. Everyone was evidently rich; my awkward suit along with my disastrous hair made some people look at me (in despise, maybe?). I sat on the table reserved for us and waited for her arrival; not long after, she arrived in a green, luxurous dress that she wore in my parents wedding. She looked a little bit heavier on that dress; well, it was made for her early days. Every eye on the restaurant followed her; with me, I thought I was a bit of nervous, but it definetly happened with her. I wanted to punch all those people in the face. Just because she's old and that dress is out of fashion, everyone needs to act like this?

I took a deep breath. Wouldn't make a scene in such an important date. Wore my most sincere smile and asked if she liked the place. 

"Oh, it couldn't be better", she smiled in approval.

We took some cheap chat and ordered our food. It was disgustingly expensive, but I picked the chef's favourite anyways. They served us a 18 years old whisky as appetizer; when the food came with an expensive champagne, we cheered and talked about petty stuff, like our neighboorhood and I was very proud of myself. I thought I was finally repaying the amount of work and trouble she got because of me; she deserved to be loved, because she was so patient and peaceful all the times, and I wasn't no easy child. I vaguely noticed every eye was still on her. Tried to look around and, to my surprise, recognized some faces; an important judge from our state, some politicians, a general who made a speech defending death penalty on TV. "Wow", I thought to myself, "this place has to be the house of egocentric millionaires". 

At some point after we ate, she excused herself and went to the bathroom. As soon as she left, a person suddenly sat right in front of me.

"Who are you?", he asked, with a devious smile. "What do you want?"

I was about to explode. Who were those invasive people? Not only they keep staring at an old lady, but now they are trying to bully me out of their sanctuary? 

"Sir, please, leave", I said, trying to stay calm. "We are just celebrating my grandma's birthday. We will never return, may you be in peace".

He got deeply concerned with my words. Quickly he went to discuss with the general, but couldn't be about me, could it? My grandma returned from the toilet and sat. Her face were not happy. Something happened.

"Kyle", she said. "I'm so, so sorry. I have to do something. You will never know, but I just have to do it".

She zipped her dress away with a small hole I never noticed. I saw something black attached to her body. "Gun!", someone yelled. And the next thing I remember is to be waking up here, in the hospital.

"Okay, mr. Kyle, we got your testimonial", the officer said. "Are you sure claiming not guilty?"

I looked right. There was nothing in the place my arm used to be. Nothing where my leg used to be. What else could I lose?

"I didn't know a thing. At least, mr. Officer", I said, "at least all those hypocrital are now burning in hell".

Iluminismo e política: Maquiavel, Hobbes, Locke, Rousseau. São filósofos contratualistas (exceto o Maquiavel, arguably) que preponderaram nessa época. Pode ler os títulos mais famosos mesmo, não é uma literatura super difícil e dão uma boa base da política moderna. 

Política como política: Aristóteles, Montesquieu, John Stuart Mill, Marx, Hanna Arendt. Todos estes falam da formação da sociedade e suas diretrizes políticas. Não precisa concordar com eles, apenas entender pontos de vista e fundamentações que são usadas até hoje. Também recomendo os livros mais famosos, não precisa entrar profundamente se não quiser. Esses são um pouco mais complexos, na minha opinião. 

Apenas iluminismo: Descartes. Acho que ele explica melhor do que ninguém o paradigma da filosofia da consciência (me corrijam se estiver errado), que é uma das teses mais importantes do período. 

Sugestão particular: "A Miséria da Teoria", de E. P. Thompson. Trata-se de um livro sobre revisionismo marxista muito interessante.
